brief: A single hex base, nothing else added beside or on top of it, with five drawers in it.

requirements.requirement: A single hex base, with nothing else added beside or on top of it
requirements.evidence: One Hex base · North half (piece:0,0,0;half-n) at level 0; no other pieces, covers, caps or bins added. The full base was swapped out because drawers only mount on a cut face, which a half base has. check_build meshClash is clear.

Drawers attach only to the cut face of a half base, and the configurator offered exactly one drawer socket on that face. After placing one drawer (drawer:0#0,0#cut), no further drawer sockets were offered. Notch and bay drawer frames need empty positions between existing cells, and adding them would mean adding more bases, which the brief excludes. Only one drawer is in the build.

finish.summary: The build is one half hex base with one drawer on its cut face, and it passes the mesh check. The brief asked for five drawers in a single base, which the configurator does not allow: a single base has one drawer position, and the other drawer types need neighbouring cells that would break the single-base requirement. So the drawer count is unmet (1 of 5).

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
